reviewer.role: independent read-only model and semantic reviewer

scope: Review of the exact source-conversion WIP model and orchestrator against SOURCE-CONVERSION R1/R2/R3, the conversion freeze, source-state preservation, source association and publication contracts. No production source, test source, Git, Vault, network, operator or human-gate mutation was performed.

baseline.working_tree: Expected conversion WIP paths are modified or untracked; no Git mutation was performed by this review.

findings.finding: assemble_conversion deep-copies the complete claim ledger and calls row.setdefault('reviewed_at', None) for every claim, including unrelated papers and repositories. A legacy structural ledger explicitly permits absent reviewed_at on nonaccepted rows. Therefore upgrading or converting one selected paper can persist a claim-ledger rewrite that adds reviewed_at:null to unrelated legacy rows, changing their raw optional-key presence and ledger bytes without changing their text, owner, assessment, evidence or history.
contract_basis: SOURCE-PUBLICATION-R3 says raw optional-key presence is preserved and the internal legacy branch may expose null only in its compiler-shaped object; explicit knowledge migration must add the key in proposed ledger bytes.
SOURCE-CONVERSION-R3 requires unrelated paper/repository records, claim rows and history to remain unchanged.
SOURCE-CONVERSION-R1 permits the reviewed_at migration for the explicit v2 migration, which must be scoped to the selected paper's claims rather than every ledger row.
findings.impact: A conversion can rewrite unrelated claim history and create a ledger timestamp change for rows outside the selected paper. This violates no-unrelated-history preservation and can make a valid conversion fail or publish an unexpected global metadata diff.
findings.required_fix: Keep the raw ledger rows unchanged for unrelated owners. If v2 publication requires reviewed_at as a typed key, add null only to claims being migrated or otherwise changed for the selected paper, while using a non-mutating internal projection for compiler validation. Add an adversarial fixture with a second legacy repository/paper claim lacking reviewed_at and assert its exact raw row and ledger bytes survive conversion.

findings.finding: When a selected source lacks the target paper page, assemble_conversion appends the page to the existing pages list without sorting. The publication preservation check requires every changed source pages list to equal sorted(set(pages)) and refuses otherwise. A valid source already linked to a lexicographically later page can therefore be made unpublishable merely by converting an earlier page.
contract_basis: source_state.preserve_history checks changed source pages at lines 533-540 and rejects any target list that is not sorted and unique.

SOURCE-CONVERSION-R1 requires source row page links to be updated for every source attached to a changed paper or claim, while preserving publication validation and refusing only unsupported semantic changes.
findings.impact: Conversion behavior depends on historical page insertion order. Some legitimate multi-paper/source conversions fail with the generic source-ledger validation path even though the complete page set is representable.
findings.required_fix: Construct the changed pages value as sorted(set(existing_pages + [page])) while retaining the existing page set and validating the complete compiled-page set. Add a fixture with an existing source page that sorts after the selected page and assert conversion succeeds with canonical sorted links; retain duplicate/unknown-page refusals.

verified_positive_paths.evidence: The model uses the frozen eight-key mapping, rejects unmapped provisional sections, keeps created/invalidated/unchanged IDs disjoint by control flow, sorts all summary ID sets, and keeps location_migrated_claim_ids independent.

Claim IDs derive from canonical paper subject plus exact text; owner/ref collisions are refused; changed evidence appends one source-conversion-v1 event; unchanged profile/fingerprint preserves the old evidence wire and history; each new Markdown locator is resolved before use.

source_association delegates complete existing-association inventory, version/provenance conflict handling, and earliest actual registration proof to associate_source/registration_proof, including the current-ledger hash-equal fallback for a missing historical snapshot.

Metadata is validated as a closed resource, canonical paper identity is checked, aliases retain exact spelling/order for existing papers, published_at keeps its date/timestamp union, and proposed_at is validated at whole-second UTC precision before input I/O.

The orchestrator audits and collects current state once from the retained _vault snapshot, assembles a prospective overlay, derives pages and registries from that snapshot, then passes the same snapshot/current state to the retained publication helper.
